rationale.Physical Exam: General Appearance: Assess how sick the patient is — obtunded.
rationale.Physical Exam: Neuro / Psych: Obtunded — neuro exam to determine impairment.
rationale.Physical Exam: Heart / Cardiovascular: Emergency — focused cardiac exam for arrhythmia.
rationale.Glucose, blood, random by glucometer: Hypo/hyperglycemia common reversible cause of AMS — check first.
rationale.ECG, 12 lead: Widened QRS + prolonged QT = TCA cardiotoxicity.
rationale.Cardiac monitor: ECG shows arrhythmia — continuous monitoring needed.
rationale.TSH: Hypothyroidism may present similarly — rule out.
rationale.CT head without contrast: Unwitnessed — rule out head trauma causing obtundation.
rationale.CPK, serum: Unknown down time — rhabdomyolysis risk. Prevent AKI.
rationale.HCG, beta (pregnancy test): Child-bearing woman — pregnancy test before radiation. Ectopic can cause this presentation.
rationale.Ethanol / Toxic alcohol panel: History suggests ethanol abuse — common co-ingestant.
rationale.Salicylate level: Aspirin is common co-ingestant in overdose.
rationale.TCA level, serum: Urine/serum positive for TCA — quantify level.
rationale.Oxygen: Low SpO2 — supplemental O2 before intubation.
rationale.Thiamine (Vitamin B1): Coma cocktail — thiamine before D50 to prevent Wernicke-Korsakoff.
rationale.Dextrose 50%: Coma cocktail — if hypoglycemic. Give thiamine first.
rationale.Naloxone: Give in any overdose to rule out reversible opioid overdose.
rationale.IV fluids (NS / LR): TCA overdose → hypotension from alpha-1 blockade. IV fluids for BP.
rationale.Nasogastric tube with suction: Prevent aspiration (intubated). Required for GI decontamination and activated charcoal.
rationale.Activated charcoal: GI decontamination if within 2 hours of ingestion. Only after airway secured. Via NG tube.
rationale.Sodium bicarbonate: For TCA cardiac toxicity (QRS >100ms, ventricular arrhythmia). Alkalinize to pH 7.45-7.55. Increases extracellular Na+ and favors non-ionized TCA.
rationale.Consult, psychiatry: Potential suicide attempt — psychiatry consult after medical stabilization.
rationale.Activated charcoal WITHOUT securing airw: NEVER give charcoal without secure airway (ETT). Risk of aspiration pneumonitis. Intubate first, then charcoal via NG.
rationale.Flumazenil: Flumazenil is contraindicated in overdose of unknown etiology — can precipitate seizures, especially with TCA co-ingestion.

hpi: {{patient_name}} is a young woman found unconscious with respiratory depression, hypotension, and altered mental status. ECG shows widened QRS, prolonged QT — classic TCA cardiotoxicity. The 'Three C's' of TCA poisoning: Coma, Convulsions, Cardiac arrhythmias. Management priorities: ABCs — intubate for airway protection (GCS depressed), mechanical ventilation. IV fluids for hypotension (TCA blocks alpha-1 receptors → vasodilation). Sodium bicarbonate for cardiac toxicity (QRS >100ms or ventricular arrhythmia) — alkalinization to pH 7.45-7.55 favors non-ionized TCA, reducing sodium channel blockade. Activated charcoal via NG tube if within 2 hours of ingestion (airway must be secured first). 'Coma cocktail': check glucose, give thiamine before D50. Naloxone for possible opioid co-ingestion. CT head to rule out trauma (unwitnessed). Aspirin and acetaminophen levels for common co-ingestants. Psychiatry consult after stabilization for suicide attempt.
